q: בן 75, הופנה על ידי רופא המשפחה לביצוע בדיקת הדמיה (MRI) במסגרת בירור ירידה קוגניטיבית הדרגתית ומתמדת במהלך השנה האחרונה. ברקע – יתר לחץ דם, סוכרת מסוג 2, ניתוח תיקון שבר בירך שמאל לפני כשנה ושבר ביד ימין לאחר נפילה לפני חודשיים. אשתו מדווחת על הפרעות שליטה על סוגר השתן מאז הנפילה והשבר בירך שמאל. בבדיקת MRI: מה הטיפול האפשרי למטופל זה?
o: DOPICAR
RIVASTIGMINE (EXELON)
ניתוח VENTRICULO-PRITONEAL SHANT
קרינה לאזור הפריאטלי מימין
explanation:
Progressive cognitive decline, gait or fall problems, urinary dysfunction and compatible ventriculomegaly raise the possibility of normal-pressure hydrocephalus. **Ventriculoperitoneal shunting** may help appropriately selected patients.

**A. Levodopa combination.** It treats dopamine-responsive parkinsonism and does not correct disturbed CSF circulation.
**B. Rivastigmine.** A cholinesterase inhibitor can have a role in selected dementias but does not drain CSF.
**C. Ventriculoperitoneal shunt.** CSF diversion is the targeted treatment. Gait assessment and response to CSF removal can inform evaluation of suitability.
**D. Right parietal radiation.** The history supplies no indication for focal radiotherapy.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 876, 913, 940.
chapterTitle: Cognitive Changes in Normal and Pathologic Aging

q: בן 87 הוא חולה נוטה למות עקב אי ספיקת לב סופנית. בעבר חתם על מינוי ייפוי כוח לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות. כעת הוא נמצא באשפוז במחלקה קרדיולוגית בשל סינקופה המיוחס לחסם הולכתי וזקוק להכנסת קוצב. מי קובע אם החולה כשיר לקבל החלטה או שיש להפעיל את מיופה הכוח?
o: רק גריאטר יכול להחליט על הוצאה מחזקת הכשרות על פי חוק החולה הנוטה למות
רופא מומחה לפי בחירת החולה ( בזמן שמילא את הטופס) יכול להחליט על הוצאה מחזקת הכשרות על פי חוק החולה הנוטה למות
רק אם הרופא האחראי הוא גריאטר או פסיכיאטר, הוא יכול להחליט על הוצאה מחזקת הכשרות
כל רופא שהוגדר כרופא אחראי יכול להוציא מחזקת הכשרות על פי חוק זה
explanation:
גם בחולה עם אי־ספיקת לב סופנית יש לברר אם הוא מבין מה הקוצב עשוי לשנות עבורו. חתימה קודמת על ייפוי כוח אינה מבטלת את חזקת הכשרות.
**הרופא שהוגדר כרופא האחראי קובע אם להוציאו מחזקת הכשרות, לאחר התייעצות, הנמקה ותיעוד.**

**א. גריאטר בלבד** אפשר להיעזר בגריאטר לבירור הגורמים לבלבול. המומחיות אינה תנאי בלעדי להכרעה.
**ב. מומחה שנבחר בטופס** בחירת מיופה כוח ועריכת הטופס אינן משנות את זהות הגורם שהחוק הסמיך לקביעת הכשרות.
**ג. רק גריאטר או פסיכיאטר בתפקיד** לרופא אחראי העונה להגדרת החוק יש סמכות גם כשהתמחותו אחרת.
**ד. רופא שהוגדר כאחראי** הוא נועץ בצוות וברופאים הרלוונטיים ובמידת האפשר ברופא האישי, ומנמק את קביעתו ברשומה.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיפים 3, 6–7, 37(ב).

chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: An 84-year-old woman receives several recommendations after comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA). After six weeks of monitoring, progress toward the agreed goals is below expectations. Her daughter reports reduced motivation. Which next step follows the CGA process?
o: Continue the existing plan with a longer observation period
Return care to the primary physician with the existing plan
Reassess the patient and revise the plan through team discussion
Increase the frequency of interventions within the existing plan
explanation:
Comprehensive geriatric assessment is a continuing process of setting goals, implementing a plan and assessing outcomes. **Reassess with the patient and team when progress falls short**.

**A. Observe longer unchanged.** This may overlook new illness, implementation barriers or changed motivation.
**B. Return unchanged plan.** Transferring care does not explain why goals were not met.
**C. Reassess and revise.** Ask what changed for the patient and agree on realistic next steps.
**D. Intensify everything.** More frequent interventions can add burden without addressing the actual barrier.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 130.
ref: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 130, Revising the treatment plan
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 130, Revising the treatment plan

q: A 90-year-old man with severe COPD on home oxygen, heart failure, and BPH presents with acute urinary retention. Catheterization drains 1.2 liters. His eGFR is 28 mL/min/1.73 m², and he takes furosemide 40 mg twice daily, metoprolol, and finasteride. His urologist proposes GreenLight laser photovaporization (PVP). Which comparison with TURP is supported by Hazzard when discussing the procedure?
o: PVP provides a tissue specimen for pathological examination after vaporization
PVP has lower transfusion rates in patients at high bleeding risk
PVP requires longer catheterization and hospitalization than TURP in the cited trial
PVP has higher reoperation requirements than TURP in the cited multicenter trial
explanation:
GreenLight photovaporization opens the prostatic outlet by vaporizing tissue. Compared with TURP, **lower transfusion rates make it worth considering when bleeding risk is high**.

**A. Provides tissue for pathology.** Vaporized tissue cannot be submitted as a resection specimen.
**B. Lower transfusion rates.** Reduced bleeding is the pertinent procedural advantage. Overall anesthetic and surgical risk still require assessment.
**C. Longer catheterization and stay.** Patients who underwent photovaporization had shorter catheterization and hospitalization in the trial.
**D. More reoperations.** Over follow-up, patients in the multicenter trial had similar overall reoperation rates after the two procedures.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 569.

q: After removal of an indwelling catheter, an older patient has persistent frequency, nocturia, and urinary leakage. His medicines were recently changed. According to Hazzard's bladder-retraining protocol, what should precede a trial of a bladder relaxant?
o: Start a bladder relaxant before investigating possible medication effects
Evaluate reversible causes and determine the postvoid residual volume
Attribute the symptoms to bladder disease before reviewing the medicines
Base treatment on voiding frequency before checking bladder emptying
explanation:
Frequency and leakage after catheter removal can reflect incomplete emptying, medicines or other reversible contributors. **Review those causes and measure postvoid residual before adding a bladder relaxant.**

**A. Start a bladder relaxant before investigating possible medication effects.** Empirical relaxation may worsen retention and overlooks recent medication changes.
**B. Evaluate reversible causes and determine the postvoid residual volume.** Residual urine distinguishes emptying failure from a primarily storage-related problem.
**C. Attribute the symptoms to bladder disease before reviewing the medicines.** Attributing symptoms to intrinsic bladder disease prematurely can miss drug effects.
**D. Base treatment on voiding frequency before checking bladder emptying.** Frequent small voids can occur with retention, so frequency alone is insufficient.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 711.

q: גבר בן 80, המוגדר חסר ישע, מאושפז שוב עקב החמרה באי־ספיקת לב. בנו אחראי למתן התרופות. אי־התאמות בטיפול ופחד של המטופל מבנו מעוררים חשד להזנחה בידי האחראי עליו. לצד בדיקה רפואית, הגנה ועירוב עובד סוציאלי, מהו סף חובת הדיווח לפקיד סעד או למשטרה המתואר בנוהל?
o: יסוד סביר לחשוב שנעברה עבירה בידי האחראי
ממצא חד־משמעי בחקירה המוכיח עבירה בידי האחראי
הודאה מתועדת של האחראי בביצוע העבירה המדוברת
הסכמה חתומה של המשפחה להעברת החשד לרשויות
explanation:
חובת דיווח נועדה לאפשר לרשויות לברר חשד לפגיעה בחסר ישע בידי אדם אחראי. **יסוד סביר לחשוב שנעברה עבירה בידי האחראי**.

**א. יסוד סביר לחשוב שנעברה עבירה בידי האחראי.** יסוד סביר מספיק להפעלת חובת הדיווח.
**ב. ממצא חד־משמעי בחקירה המוכיח עבירה בידי האחראי.** הוכחה פלילית היא תוצאה אפשרית של חקירה.
**ג. הודאה מתועדת של האחראי בביצוע העבירה המדוברת.** אין להתנות הגנה על הנפגע בהודאת החשוד.
**ד. הסכמה חתומה של המשפחה להעברת החשד לרשויות.** הסכמת המשפחה אינה תנאי לדיווח הקבוע בדין.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 2, 6, סעיפים 1.2, 8, 9.

q: An 80-year-old woman with severe knee osteoarthritis has recurrent pain rated 7/10 that limits shopping. A course of three hyaluronic acid injections six months ago initially helped. She has heart failure with an ejection fraction of 35% and stage 3b CKD, and takes furosemide, lisinopril, and carvedilol. Examination shows an effusion and crepitus. She is reluctant to undergo the knee replacement recommended by her surgeon. Which injectable option has evidence for symptomatic relief in Hazzard, while the other choices are described as lacking clear benefit or remaining experimental?
o: Intra-articular injection using hyaluronic acid
Intra-articular injection using a glucocorticoid
Intra-articular injection using platelet-rich plasma
Intra-articular injection using mesenchymal stem cells
explanation:
Intra-articular glucocorticoid injection can provide short-term relief for a persistently painful osteoarthritic knee. **A glucocorticoid injection** is a reasonable local option with an effusion, after evaluating for other causes of swelling.

**A. Hyaluronic acid.** Her prior subjective relief matters to the discussion, but controlled evidence of consistent benefit is unclear.
**B. Glucocorticoid.** Local anti-inflammatory action can improve symptoms without the systemic kidney and heart-failure risks of an oral NSAID.
**C. Platelet-rich plasma.** Preparations vary, and expected pain relief is less predictable than with an intra-articular glucocorticoid.
**D. Mesenchymal stem cells.** These remain experimental for this indication and are not the established pain-relieving injection.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 788–789.

q: A 77-year-old woman with HFpEF (EF 58%), type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and biopsy-proven transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis has NYHA class II symptoms despite furosemide 40 mg daily, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Echocardiography shows LV wall thickening and grade 2 diastolic dysfunction. Which treatment is the TTR stabilizer described in Hazzard as reducing mortality versus placebo in ATTR-ACT?
o: Metoprolol as the TTR-stabilizing treatment
Spironolactone as the TTR-stabilizing treatment
Tafamidis as the TTR-stabilizing treatment
Sacubitril/valsartan as the TTR-stabilizing treatment
explanation:
In ATTR cardiomyopathy unstable transthyretin tetramers dissociate and contribute to amyloid deposition. **Tafamidis stabilizes the tetramer and improved survival in ATTR-ACT**.

**A. Metoprolol** A beta blocker affects heart rate and adrenergic signaling. It has no TTR-stabilizing action.
**B. Spironolactone** It blocks the mineralocorticoid receptor and does not modify the amyloid protein.
**C. Tafamidis** The lower all-cause mortality and slower functional decline were observed in patients with transthyretin cardiomyopathy.
**D. Sacubitril/valsartan** This combines neprilysin inhibition and angiotensin receptor blockade. Neither component stabilizes TTR.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1188. ATTR-ACT (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1805689).

q: An older man with hypertension and a previous myocardial infarction is being considered for a beta-blocker. Which consideration supports its use according to Hazzard?
o: Secondary prevention after a previous myocardial infarction
Its role as monotherapy for uncomplicated hypertension
Its role in reducing peripheral vascular resistance
Its role in preventing adverse metabolic effects
explanation:
Among these considerations, **a prior myocardial infarction can provide a separate cardiovascular indication for beta blockade**. Recency of the infarct, LV function, angina and other indications matter when deciding on long-term use.

**A. Secondary prevention after MI.** Beta blockade is especially relevant after recent MI or with reduced LV systolic function.
**B. Uncomplicated hypertension alone.** In an older adult without another indication, other antihypertensive classes are generally preferred as initial monotherapy.
**C. Peripheral vasodilation.** This is not the primary action of most beta blockers, although some agents have vasodilating properties.
**D. Protection from metabolic effects.** Some beta blockers can mask hypoglycemia or affect metabolic parameters.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1226. AHA/ACC Guideline for Chronic Coronary Disease, 2023.

q: A 77-year-old woman has ulcerative colitis in remission on mesalamine 800 mg three times daily. Over 3 months, she has developed straining and a bowel movement every 4 days. She also takes weekly alendronate and vitamin D, and recently started amitriptyline 10 mg for peripheral neuropathy. There is no abdominal tenderness. Which mechanism explains the constipating effect of an anticholinergic medication?
o: Enhanced smooth-muscle contraction through muscarinic stimulation
Reduced smooth-muscle contraction through antimuscarinic activity
Increased stool water through chloride-channel activation
Increased propulsive activity through serotonin-receptor stimulation
explanation:
Muscarinic signaling helps intestinal smooth muscle contract. Amitriptyline blocks that signal, so **reduced smooth-muscle contraction slows transit**.

**A. Enhanced smooth-muscle contraction through muscarinic stimulation.** Muscarinic stimulation increases contraction, opposite to an anticholinergic drug's effect.
**B. Reduced smooth-muscle contraction through antimuscarinic activity.** Blocking muscarinic receptors reduces propulsive contraction and contributes to constipation.
**C. Increased stool water through chloride-channel activation.** Chloride-channel activation draws water into the bowel and is used to treat constipation.
**D. Increased propulsive activity through serotonin-receptor stimulation.** Stimulation of selected serotonin receptors can promote propulsion, the opposite direction.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1358, 1377.

q: An older man with Alzheimer disease develops confusion, dry mouth, and constipation after starting oxybutynin. Which explanation is consistent with the drug effects listed in Hazzard?
o: A cholinergic drug effect involving cognition and gastrointestinal function
An anticholinergic drug effect involving cognition and gastrointestinal function
A cholinergic drug effect associated with improvement in constipation
An anticholinergic drug effect associated with improvement in delirium
explanation:
Oxybutynin blocks muscarinic receptors in the bladder and can have systemic effects. **Anticholinergic cognitive and gastrointestinal adverse effects** explain new confusion, dry mouth and constipation in this man with Alzheimer disease.

**A. Cholinergic stimulation.** This is the opposite of oxybutynin's mechanism.
**B. Anticholinergic effect.** Less salivary secretion and bowel motility occur alongside possible impairment of attention or cognition.
**C. Cholinergic relief of constipation.** Oxybutynin slows the bowel and can worsen constipation.
**D. Anticholinergic improvement in delirium.** Central anticholinergic exposure can provoke or worsen delirium.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 712.

q: A 78-year-old man with CLL takes ibrutinib 420 mg/day. He also has hypertension treated with lisinopril 10 mg and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 45); he takes aspirin 81 mg. He presents with three weeks of progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea and five days of dark stools. He is pale, with BP 128/78, heart rate 96, no orthostatic changes, and no lymphadenopathy. Hemoglobin is 6.8 g/dL (baseline 11.2), MCV 82, platelets 165,000, WBC 42,000 with 85% lymphocytes, and creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (baseline 1.4). He has received one unit of packed red cells and is hemodynamically stable. Which statement about ibrutinib is relevant to reviewing his bleeding risk?
o: It reduces bleeding propensity, so concurrent antiplatelet therapy is reassuring
It increases bleeding propensity, requiring antiplatelet risk-benefit review
It increases bleeding propensity, making concurrent antiplatelet therapy protective
It reduces bleeding propensity, making a medication contribution less concerning
explanation:
Ibrutinib can impair platelet function even when the platelet count is normal. With melena and a major hemoglobin fall, **review the additive bleeding risk of ibrutinib and aspirin** while evaluating the gastrointestinal bleed.

**A. Reassurance from antiplatelet use.** Aspirin can add to a drug-related platelet defect.
**B. Increased bleeding, review aspirin.** Reassess the indication for each medicine and the risks of interruption or continuation.
**C. Aspirin protects against bleeding.** Platelet inhibition cannot protect against hemorrhage in this combination.
**D. Reduced bleeding tendency.** Ibrutinib increases concern for bleeding even with a platelet count of 165,000.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1497.
ref: Hazzard Ch 95 — HEMATOLOGIC MALIGNANCIES (LEUKEMIA/LYMPHOMA) AND PLASMA CELL DISORDERS
chapterTitle: Hematologic Malignancies (Leukemia/Lymphoma) and Plasma Cell Disorders

q: בת 80 הגיעה למרפאה למעקב של צפיפות העצם. מטופלת ב- ALENDRONATE 70 מ"ג פעם בשבוע מזה 7 שנים בשל אוסטאופורוזיס. בבדיקת צפיפות העצם T-SCORE -2.22.בצוואר ירך ימין. ללא היסטוריה של שברים, ללא ירידה בגובה, ללא היסטוריה משפחתית של שברים בירך. מה מהאפשרויות הבאות היא הניהול המתאים ביותר לבריאות העצם שלה ?
o: להמשך טיפול ב- ALENDRONATE
להמשיך טיפול ב- ALENDRONATE ולהוסיף טיפול ב- TERIPARATIDE (FORTEO)
להפסיק טיפול ב- ALENDRONATE
להפסיק טיפול ב- ALENDRONATE ולתת טיפול ב- TERIPARATIDE (FORTEO)
explanation:
Bisphosphonates persist in bone, permitting a monitored treatment holiday for some patients after prolonged therapy. **Reassess fracture risk and consider pausing alendronate** after seven years if she is now at low or moderate risk.

**A. Continue alendronate.** Appropriate if current overall risk remains high. Age, falls, prior fractures and density all matter.
**B. Add teriparatide.** No multiple fractures or very-high-risk features are supplied to justify this escalation.
**C. Pause alendronate.** No prior fracture and a current hip T-score of minus 2.22 support considering a holiday, with subsequent monitoring.
**D. Switch immediately to teriparatide.** Stopping prolonged bisphosphonate therapy is not by itself an indication for an anabolic drug.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 777.

q: בת 75 אובחנה עם היצרות חמורה של המסתם האאורטאלי לאחר בירור של כאבים בחזה. איזה מהשיקולים הבאים בבחירת הטיפול המתאים בין Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) ל- Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement (SAVR) הוא הנכון ומדוע?
o: ביצוע TAVR בנוכחות סימני אי ספיקת לב כי צפוי שיפור משמעותי יותר בתסמינים
ביצוע SAVR לאחר הקרנות לבית החזה בעבר כי יש סיכוי נמוך יותר להתערבות חוזרת
ביצוע TAVR אם יש ריבוי מחלות רקע כי מפחית סיכון להשתלת קוצב
ביצוע SAVR אם יש מחלה קורונרית תלת כלית כי ניתן לבצע 2 התערבויות בבת אחת
explanation:
In severe aortic stenosis with **three-vessel coronary disease suitable for CABG, SAVR permits valve replacement and bypass during one operation**. A Heart Team should still assess anatomy, frailty, operative risk and goals.

**A. TAVR for greater symptom improvement.** Both procedures can relieve obstruction. Heart failure alone does not guarantee greater symptom relief with TAVR.
**B. SAVR after chest radiation.** Prior radiation can increase surgical risk or make open access difficult. It does not inherently favor surgery.
**C. TAVR to reduce pacemaker risk.** TAVR can injure the conduction system and increase the need for permanent pacing.
**D. SAVR with multivessel CABG.** Concomitant surgical revascularization is a concrete reason to favor a combined operation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 75, p. 1153.
